nonclaim: This V3 record checks one exact externally frozen Ferric, tuned vLLM, and tuned SGLang comparison roster, retains an ordered event for every successful request, requires identical per-request input/output work across engines in each aligned window, and recomputes end-to-end latency, TTFT, TPOT, token throughputs, nearest-rank percentiles, exact medians, fastest-baseline selection, and a deterministic paired-percentile-bootstrap 95% throughput interval. TPOT is floor((terminal-first-token)/(output-tokens-1)) nanoseconds per output token and therefore requires at least two output tokens per request. The record enforces declared p99 timing SLOs and a 0.95 throughput lower confidence bound. It does not validate the external plan, versions, sources, tuning choices, budget, SLO choice, event truth, server freshness, hardware behavior, numerical correctness, or independent reproduction; it is not qualification evidence and does not close m1.r33 or M1.

schema.arithmetic: Each engine window carries positive duration_ns, successful_requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, and total_tokens plus zero failed_requests and one ordered event per successful request. Checked window and event token sums must agree. End-to-end is terminal-arrival nanoseconds, TTFT is first-token-arrival nanoseconds, and TPOT is floor((terminal-first-token)/(output-tokens-1)) nanoseconds per output token after the first. The checker recomputes nearest-rank p50, p90, and p99 for every timing metric. Each input, output, or total rate is floor(the corresponding token count*1000000000/duration_ns). Even medians are exact reduced rationals. The fastest baseline is the larger median total-token rate, with vLLM winning a tie. The comparison ratio is floor(Ferric_median_total_rate/baseline_median_total_rate*1000000). Ten thousand paired resamples of the thirty aligned recorded total-token-rate windows use SplitMix64 seeded by the SHA-256 identity of a V3 domain-separated policy and observation digest pair. The nearest-rank 250th and 9750th sorted estimates form the deterministic percentile-bootstrap 95% interval, and its lower bound must be at least 950000 PPM.
schema.bindings: The V3 policy freezes exact plan, executable, environment, Ferric and fe2o3 source closures, model, tokenizer, weights, schedule, workload, trace, output-limit, implementation, protocol, source, config, tuning, and equal tuning-budget SHA-256 identities before observation. V1 and V2 policy, observation, record, and protocol formats and authorities are not reinterpreted as V3.
schema.order: Exactly three starts appear in ascending order. Each contains ten ordered warmup windows followed by ten ordered recorded windows. Every window carries the exact cyclic Ferric/vLLM/SGLang execution order and all three event-backed metric sets.
schema.output: The checker rereads an exclusive held sibling staging file, publishes with renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE, synchronizes the parent, and finally rebinds and rereads the published pathname. The V3 record carries exact policy bindings, raw rows and request events, input SHA-256 identities, recomputed p50/p90/p99 E2E/TTFT/TPOT summaries, input/output/total-token median throughputs, fastest baseline, Ferric total-throughput ratio, bootstrap seed identity, and paired-bootstrap interval. Submitted summaries are outside the input schema.
schema.pairing: Every row has one cyclic engine order and all three engines retain ascending request ordinals from zero. Successful-request counts and aggregate work must match, and each aligned request ordinal must carry identical positive input-token and output-token work across Ferric, vLLM, and SGLang. Arrival offsets need not be byte-equal because each engine executes the frozen trace in a distinct sequential window.
schema.timing: Each event uses monotonic-raw-nanoseconds offsets from its declared window start and carries arrival_offset_ns, first_token_offset_ns, and terminal_offset_ns with arrival < first-token < terminal <= duration. End-to-end and TTFT are in nanoseconds. TPOT is in nanoseconds per output token after the first and requires at least two output tokens. The V3 checker recomputes every submitted percentile from the retained events and rejects any drift.
